archetype.name: Retooling (possession without finish)
archetype.definition: A Calgary team two years removed from its last good season, still building around young pieces like Zayne Parekh, that holds the puck well enough but has neither the finishing nor the goaltending to turn it into wins.

report.headline: A .500-ish record hiding a last-place offense and a goaltending collapse
report.take:
Calgary sits 10-12-2, sixth in the Pacific and 18th on the site's Teams tab. That is a better spot than the underlying season deserves. The Flames have been outscored by 24 goals, the 30th-worst margin per game in the league. Their 2.5 goals a game ranks dead last. Pts vs Goal Diff credits them with 3.1 standings points beyond what their goals imply, third-most in the NHL. Three of the last ten games went to overtime, and so did a 2-1 win in San Jose. The record has been propped up by surviving close games, not by winning them on the margin.

The cause is clear when you split the ice. With the puck, Calgary is fine: a 51% CF %, eighth in the league, and a power play converting 26.3%, fifth. But possession hasn't produced danger. The xGF % of 47.4% ranks 24th, so the Flames carry the puck without getting to the good ice. Then the finishing craters. Skaters are shooting 7.8% against a league mark of 9.8%, and the 5-on-5 PDO sits at 96.5. In net, the team that posted Goalies GSAx of 16.7 and 14.2 the last two seasons is at -4.7. That earns a D- grade.

The goaltending split is the story inside the story. Dustin Wolf has 13 starts at a .877 Save % and -6.6 GSAx, 67th of 72 on the goalie tab. Devin Cooley has 10 starts at .906 and +1.5 GSAx. The defensive structure in front of them isn't the problem. The blueline grades B+, and Calgary holds opposing forwards 0.21 points a game under their norms, seventh-best. Wingers, though, take half the points scored against them, against a league share of 43%.

Some of the low PDO should fade upward, especially the shooting. Yet the xGF % says the shooting is low partly because the chances are poor, and last season's 47% xGF and 32nd-ranked offense say this isn't new. Expect the scoring to improve modestly and the close-game luck to drift the other way. Net, that leaves a team living in the high-70s points range, close to last year's 77 and short of a playoff spot.

strengths.title: Power play punching above weight
strengths.body: At 26.3%, the power play runs well above the league's 22.5% and is the most reliable offense this team has. Parekh drives it from the point with 5 of his 10 points on the man advantage. After last season's 16.2%, some fade is possible. But it is the one unit that consistently turns possession into goals.

strengths.title: Puck possession and penalty killing
strengths.body: An eighth-ranked CF % and an 80.8% PK, 11th in the league, show a team that isn't getting run off the ice. Forwards against them sit well under their expected output, consistent with a B+ blueline. This floor is structural and should hold.

concerns.title: League-worst offense, chance-poor possession
concerns.body: Calgary scores 2.5 goals a game, 32nd, and 0.7 below the league rate. The 7.8% shooting is unlucky, but a 47.4% xGF % means the shots aren't dangerous either, and last season's offense also ranked 32nd. Expect a little bounce in finishing, not a transformation.

concerns.title: Wolf's season in net
concerns.body: The goaltending has swung from a strength in each of the last two seasons to a D-. That collapse sits almost entirely with Wolf's .877 and -6.6 GSAx, while Cooley has been above expected. How the starts are split may matter more than any skater.

concerns.title: Record ahead of the goals
concerns.body: The goal differential of -24 is bottom-three territory. Yet the Flames hold 3.1 points more than their goals imply. Overtime results and one-goal wins rarely stay this kind, so the standings position is softer than it looks.

trend.note: After a 6-8 October with 3.71 goals allowed a game, November has tightened defensively to 3.2 allowed a game. But the scoring has stayed stuck near 2.4. The last 10 games went 4-4-2, a .500 points pace that matches who they've been all year.

weekAhead.headline: Four-game eastern road trip, three against winning teams
weekAhead.body:
Calgary heads east for four straight road games: Ottawa, Pittsburgh, New Jersey and the Rangers. Three of them carry winning records. Only Pittsburgh, 7-14-2 and 28th on the site, looks like a clear chance. For a team scoring last in the league, the trip's swing comes down to the power play and to which goalie starts.

Ottawa (15-6-3) and New Jersey (15-8-0) out-chance opponents at elite rates, with xGF % in the league's top five. Both, however, have soft spots Calgary's strengths can hit: Ottawa's power play is 32nd, and New Jersey's PK is 30th. The Rangers close it out with the league's best PK and Save %. Calgary already lost to them 3-1 at home this month.

keyMatchups.title: Flames power play vs Devils PK
keyMatchups.body: New Jersey kills just 64.2% of penalties, 30th in the league, and its goaltending grades D at -9.4 GSAx. Calgary's 26.3% power play is the best chance on the trip to manufacture goals the even-strength game won't produce. Draw penalties in that game and the offense problem eases for a night.

keyMatchups.title: Rangers goaltending shuts the door
keyMatchups.body: New York leads the league in Save % at .917 and in PK % at 90%, with an A- goaltending grade. Against a team shooting 7.8%, that is the worst possible finish to the trip. The Rangers do concede shot attempts (47% CF %), so Calgary will have the puck. Scoring with it is the question.

keyMatchups.title: Pittsburgh's leaky middle
keyMatchups.body: The Penguins have a blueline graded F and let centers score 0.19 points a game above expectation, 31st in the league. This is the most winnable game of the week. Calgary's forwards need to cash in, because the other three opponents won't give as much.

weekAhead.watch: Who gets the starts: Cooley's .906 versus Wolf's .877 is the difference between stealing a point or two on this trip and coming home empty.

restOfSeason.body:
The shooting percentage should drift back toward normal, adding a bit of offense. The power play and possession game give the Flames a floor most bottom-ten teams lack. But the chance quality is below average and has been for two seasons, so the ceiling is limited. The overtime and close-game cushion that has kept the record near .500 is more likely to shrink than grow.

If the goaltending returns toward what this team got the past two years, a .500-plus run is possible and the Flames hover near the Pacific's wildcard mix. If Wolf keeps playing at this level and the starts don't shift, they finish around the 75-point pace. My range for final points is 72 to 84, closer to the low end. Expect goals a game to settle around 2.6 to 2.9.

projections.stat: Goals scored / game, rest of season

swingFactors: Wolf's save percentage recovering or Cooley taking the net
Shooting % regressing up toward league average
Power play sustaining a top-five rate

confidence.note: 24 games is enough for the possession and chance-share picture, less so for shooting and save percentages.
